# Temple Scroll Column 47 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 47 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**47:1** If a woman marries while her vows or her rash promises are still in effect —

**47:2** and her husband hears about them and says nothing on the day he finds out — her vows remain valid, and her commitments stand.

**47:3** But if her husband cancels them on the day he finds out, the LORD will release her.

**47:4** A widow or divorced woman is bound by every vow and commitment she makes.

**47:5** These are the rules the LORD gave about vows between husband and wife, and between a father and his young daughter living at home.

**47:6** When a man or woman makes a special vow — the Nazirite vow — dedicating themselves to the LORD,

**47:7** they must stay away from wine and beer. They must not drink wine vinegar or beer vinegar, or any grape juice, or eat fresh or dried grapes.

**47:8** For the entire time of their dedication, they must not eat anything that comes from a grapevine, not even the seeds or skins.

**47:9** For the entire time of their Nazirite vow, no razor may touch their head. Until the dedication period is complete, they are holy. They must let their hair grow freely.

**47:10** For the entire time of their dedication to the LORD, they must not go near a dead body.

**47:11** They must stay away from wine and beer; they must not drink vinegar made from wine or beer, and they must not drink any grape juice.

**47:12** Even if their father, mother, brother, or sister dies, they must not make themselves unclean. The mark of their dedication to God is on their head.

**47:13** For the entire time of their dedication, they are holy to the LORD.

**47:14** If someone suddenly dies right next to them, contaminating their consecrated head, they must shave their head on the day of purification — the seventh day.

**47:15** On the eighth day they must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

**47:16** The priest will offer one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering, making atonement for the person because of the contamination from the dead body. That day they must reconsecrate their head.

---

*PNEUMA notes: This column wraps up the women's vow legislation and introduces the Nazirite vow (Numbers 6). The Nazirite takes on three dramatic restrictions: no grape products at all (not even seeds or skins), no haircuts, and no contact with the dead — even family members. This represents a voluntary, temporary taking on of priestly-level holiness. The accidental contamination provision shows practical realism alongside the idealism.*
